data.claim: A controller decides a live lane's kill in one switch: a soft unwind (hard=false) preserves the worktree and a hard kill (hard=true, salvageable=False) discards it, and a hard kill over an adopted tree or an unmeasured tree falls back to soft
data.falsifier: tests/test_lanes_kill_unwind.py fails: decide(hard=True, salvageable=False).preserve is True, or decide(hard=True, adopted=True).preserve is False
data.mechanism: a pure decide(item, lane, *, hard, adopted, salvageable) mirrors recover_auto: every kill stops the subagent and releases the lease, only worktree disposal differs; guardrails refuse a discard of an adopted or unmeasured tree
data.question: Kill-unwind switch: can soft unwind and hard kill be one pure decision for a live lane?

evidence.note: research Rcc608467d3 CONFIRMED: the kill-unwind switch is one pure decide(); 7 tests pass (tests/test_lanes_kill_unwind.py), refuting the falsifier.

Work-queue rules followed: claimed before editing (isolated worktree), worked in the worktree, record-as-you-go (research Rcc608467d3). The four enforced rules hold: no unavailable recorded as passed; unmeasurable/partial never pass; reviews come from another model family (grok xai + gemini google); no bug is closed without a regression test (this is a feature item, no bug).

Added ddflow/services/lanes/unwind.py (the pure kill-unwind switch: SOFT=soft_unwind preserves, HARD=hard_kill discards; decide(item,lane,*,hard,adopted,salvageable); guardrails fall back to soft over adopted/unmeasured trees; decisions() mirrors recover_auto.decisions) and tests/test_lanes_kill_unwind.py (7 tests). Module is the ACTIVE counterpart of recover_auto (passive corpse recovery).

chunk_findings.detail: Given `hard=True`, `adopted=False`, and `salvageable=True`, `decide` returns `effect=HARD`, `hard=True`, `preserve=False`. The docstring says a hard kill discards the worktree only when the tree is “measured discardable,” but `salvageable=True` is a measured answer that the tree is salvageable—the opposite of discardable. Thus a controller that measures a live worktree as salvageable and requests a hard kill will still discard it, ignoring the boolean value and only treating `None` as unmeasured. This can throw away recoverable work that the stated guardrail should preserve.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/unwind.py:95

chunk_findings.detail:
The `decide` function signature accepts `salvageable: bool | None = None`, but the documentation and logic imply that a value of `True` (salvageable worktree) behaves differently from `False` (discardable worktree). However, looking at the implementation:
```python
    if salvageable is None:
        return Kill(
            item,
            lane,
            SOFT,
            "hard kill asked, the worktree could not be measured...",
            False,
            True,
        )
    return Kill(
        item,
        lane,
        HARD,
        "hard kill: stop the subagent, release the lease, and discard the worktree...",
        True,
        False,
    )
```
When `salvageable=True` (meaning the worktree contains valuable or uncommitted work that should *not* be discarded), the function still falls through and returns `HARD`, which discards the worktree (`preserve=False`). This means passing `salvageable=True` to `decide(..., hard=True, salvageable=True)` incorrectly treats a salvageable worktree as discardable, violating the guardrail that salvageable work should be preserved.

data.summary: ddflow recover labels an item [expired_lease] and ddflow lanes shows 'stopped (reason unknown)' even when the lease already auto-released and the item's worktree is clean-and-fully-merged. release --note salvaged is then a no-op ('no lease'), so the label is stale relative to the item's actual state; a clean merged item should read done, not [expired_lease]. This makes the recovery/lane surface overstate crash-orphans and understate finished work (buglane19/fix-B682472298e case).

data.body:
Fixes bug Ba73b94a6ad: ddflow recover labels an item [expired_lease] and ddflow lanes shows 'stopped (reason unknown)' even when the lease already auto-released and the item's worktree is clean-and-fully-merged. release --note salvaged is then a no-op ('no lease'), so the label is stale relative to the item's actual state; a clean merged item should read done, not [expired_lease]. This makes the recovery/lane surface overstate crash-orphans and understate finished work (buglane19/fix-B682472298e case).

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Ba73b94a6ad --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Ba73b94a6ad --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug Ba73b94a6ad: ddflow recover labels an item [expired_lease] and ddflow lanes shows 'stopped (reason unknown)'...
